To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the set of all conversations generated by an e-service composed of Mealy peers is context sensitive and that the set of allowed conversations can be specified by conversation specifications.

the global behaviors of e-service compositions are not always regular, that the local behaviors of peers can be regular even if the global behavior is not, and that a regular language can be realized by Mealy peers in a composition if and only if the composition has a certain shape.

(a) the set of conversations exhibited by a composite e-service can be quite complicated, (b) the local prepone operator can be used to simulate the effect of queuing delays from the global point of view, (c) the local projection operator can be used in a converse manner to reflect the local point of view, and (d) the set of all conversations exhibited by a Mealy e-service has a natural closure under local prepone and local projection.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the set of global conversations of a Mealy composition is the local prep one and projection-join of a regular language if and only if the Mealy peers have a certain shape.

for a given e-service composition, there exists a Mealy implementation that realizes the conversations specified by a given conversation specification if and only if the set of conversations specified is the local prep one and projection-join of a regular language and the shape of the composition is as required in the second result.

the sets of conversations of Mealy peers can be characterized by a regular language (and a Mealy machine), and the sets of conversations generated by e-service compositions are regular (and can be realized by Mealy machines).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a formal framework for specifying the behavior of e-service composition, and have studied the relationship between the global behavior of a composition and the local behavior of its individual components.
the sets of conversations of e-service compositions exhibit a wide range of behaviors, but we are able to capture the most interesting ones by our framework.
the set of all conversations of Mealy e-service composition is always context-sensitive, and the set of all conversation specifications of Mealy e-services is regular.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a conversation specification is an effective way to describe the global behavior of a composition.
e-service composition is inherently non-regular.
the global behavior of a composition of e-services is a rich language that is more expressive than the composition of the local behaviors of its peers.
